entry.title: New planet candidate: TIC 8890043
entry.summary: The signal is a repeating dip in starlight occurring every 9.584 days, which suggests a planet about 1.6 times the size of Earth is passing in front of the star. While the signal is quite strong with a high signal-to-noise ratio, we must be cautious because there is a nearby star of similar brightness within the camera's pixels that could be causing a false reading. When looking at the plots, focus on the light curve to see if the three dips are consistent and check the centroid offset to ensure the light is actually coming from the target star and not the neighbor.

entry.title: New planet candidate: TIC 372951467

When looking at the plots, check the light curve for the consistent timing of the dips and inspect the "centroid offset" to see if the light source shifts toward that nearby star during the transit.

entry.title: [Black holes & extreme events] Gravitational waves hint at black holes born from failed supernovae
entry.summary: New evidence from gravitational waves suggests some black holes are created when massive stars fail to explode as supernovae. Instead of a big explosion, the star's core simply collapses into a black hole.

entry.title: [Galaxies & cosmology] First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
entry.summary: Scientists have completed the first direct measurement of how cosmic hydrogen is clustered across the universe. This new data could change the way researchers map the large-scale structure of space.

entry.title: [Black holes & extreme events] Science Release: Astronomers Discover Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the Oldest Compact Quasar Pair in the Universe
entry.summary: Astronomers have found the oldest pair of compact quasars ever seen, located just 900 million years after the Big Bang. These two massive, feeding black holes are so large that scientists do not yet have a theory to explain how they grew so fast.

entry.title: [Black holes & extreme events] Early Supermassive Black Holes Aren’t All Monsters
entry.summary: Researchers searched for hidden supermassive black holes that existed in the early universe. The study suggests that these early black holes are not all as massive as previously thought.

entry.title: [Missions & launches] NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
entry.summary: NASA scientists are studying how the future LISA observatory will use gravitational waves to find new worlds. These waves are tiny ripples in space-time caused by large objects orbiting each other.

entry.title: [Missions & launches] A robot just built a structure autonomously in space for the 1st time ever
entry.summary: A robot has successfully built a structure in space on its own for the first time. This technology could be used to assemble large telescopes or other equipment in orbit without humans.

entry.title: [Exoplanets] Atmosphere of lava planet: ‘A cloudy, reflective sunscreen’
entry.summary: The Webb telescope has observed a super-Earth called TOI-561 b, which is a planet covered in lava. The observations show that the planet has a very reflective and cloudy atmosphere.

entry.title: [Other] Twin gas rings observed around a white dwarf
entry.summary: Astronomers have discovered two gas rings surrounding a white dwarf star. These rings are shaped like twins around the dead star.

entry.title: [Stars] The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
entry.summary: Astronomers used the JWST to find a very cold, tiny object known as a Y dwarf. By measuring its movement over two years, they proved it is the most distant ultra-cold dwarf ever found.

entry.title: [Stars] The supernova impostor: Chandra finds likely source of giant star's repeated outbursts
entry.summary: The Chandra X-ray Observatory has identified what causes a giant, unstable star to have repeated outbursts. This star is sometimes called a 'supernova impostor' because of its behavior.

entry.title: [Black holes & extreme events] Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
entry.summary: Scientists are investigating small, red objects called Little Red Dots found by the James Webb Space Telescope. New research suggests these might actually be tiny black holes created during the Big Bang.

entry.title: [Exoplanets] Expanding the Volatile Abundance Inventory for High-Priority K-Dwarf JWST Exoplanet Systems
entry.summary: Scientists studied the chemical makeup of six stars that have planets orbiting them. They measured how much carbon and oxygen these stars contain to help understand their planetary systems.

entry.title: [Other] Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
entry.summary: Researchers studied what would happen to satellites in low Earth orbit if a nuclear weapon were detonated in space. They found that the radiation could disable almost all satellites in the area within one week.

entry.title: [Asteroids & comets] Our sun's undiscovered stellar nemesis is still out there, says physicist
entry.summary: Physicists are discussing the possibility of dangerous comets that could cause mass extinctions on Earth. These comets are thought to come from a massive, spherical cloud of icy objects called the Oort cloud.

entry.title: [Planets & moons] A Perseverance Experiment Could Help Astronauts Prepare for Dust Storms on Mars
entry.summary: Scientists studied how Martian dust interacts with materials on the Perseverance Rover. This research helps planners understand how dust might affect future astronauts and their equipment on Mars.

entry.title: [Asteroids & comets] Long-lived mineral grains can be invaluable for reconstructing impact events, but the stories are complex
entry.summary: Scientists use long-lived mineral grains to study past impact events on Earth and the moon. These grains help researchers understand how the solar system and planets have changed over time.

entry.title: [Exoplanets] Two nearby rocky worlds could offer alien astronomers views of planets appearing to reverse course
entry.summary: Scientists are studying how two nearby rocky planets might look to alien astronomers. These planets could appear to move backward in their orbits from a different perspective.

entry.title: [Sun & space weather] Exploring Coronal Mass Ejections with Synthetic Spacecraft
entry.summary: New research uses synthetic spacecraft to study how coronal mass ejections work. The study shows that the path a spacecraft takes changes how we understand these solar eruptions.

entry.title: [Other] The Low-α Splash Population in the Milky Way
entry.summary: Scientists are using models to study a specific group of stars in the Milky Way called the 'Splash' population. These stars have unique chemical properties and move in unusual orbits.

entry.title: [Missions & launches] NASA’s ESCAPADE Completes Powered Earth Flybys, Now En Route to Mars
entry.summary: Two ESCAPADE spacecraft successfully completed powered flybys of Earth. They used Earth's gravity and engine burns to help them travel toward Mars.

entry.title: [Other] Hot gas in Cygnus
entry.summary: A nebula in the Cygnus constellation surrounds the Wolf-Rayet star WR 134. The star's strong winds are creating a bright bubble in the surrounding gas about 6,000 light-years away.

entry.title: [Missions & launches] The Vera C. Rubin Observatory, making a 10-year time-lapse of the night sky
entry.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory is using a ground-based telescope to create a 10-year time-lapse of the sky. This project will help scientists study dark matter, dark energy, and objects in our Solar System.

entry.title: [Planets & moons] Mysterious gas on Mars suggests magma below
entry.summary: Researchers found hydrogen chloride gas leaking from the ground near a large volcano on Mars. This discovery suggests that active magma might be buried underneath the surface.

entry.title: [Other] A Stellar Odd Couple at an Unusual Stage of Evolution
entry.summary: Astronomers are studying a pair of stars where one is a millisecond pulsar and the other is becoming a white dwarf. The pulsar pulls material from its companion star, which speeds up the companion's evolution.

entry.title: [Missions & launches] NASA unveils $10 billion in moon base contracts, new lunar missions and the 'PROMISE' of a nuclear-powered rover
entry.summary: NASA has announced $10 billion in contracts to help build a moon base by 2032. These plans include new lunar missions and a nuclear-powered rover.

entry.title: [Astrobiology] CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars
entry.summary: Four volunteers have finished a 378-day simulation of living on Mars. They lived inside the Mars Dune Alpha habitat without windows or real-time contact with the outside world.

entry.title: [Sun & space weather] Sun news: Auroras continue! More tonight at northern U.S. latitudes?
entry.summary: Fast solar winds reaching speeds over 800 km/s are causing solar storms. These storms may create auroras visible in the northern United States tonight.

entry.title: [Black holes & extreme events] ATel 18146: XMM-Newton detection of hard X-ray emission from the nearby Type Ia-CSM SN 2026sqf
entry.summary: Astronomers used the XMM-Newton telescope to detect X-rays from a nearby supernova called SN 2026sqf. This supernova is located in the galaxy NGC 3310.

entry.title: [Galaxies & cosmology] Nearby Dwarf Galaxies Show Surprising Lack Of Oxygen, Says Paper
entry.summary: A study of over 36 dwarf galaxies found they contain much less oxygen than expected. This finding suggests there are still things scientists do not understand about how galaxies grow.

entry.title: [Galaxies & cosmology] JWST tracks more than 100 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy
entry.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope found 104 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy. This is more than double the previous record of 44 events.

entry.title: [Astrobiology] Game theory helps SETI search for alien civilizations
entry.summary: Scientists are using game theory to improve the search for signs of alien civilizations. This method helps decide where to look for technosignatures from other intelligent life.

entry.title: [Black holes & extreme events] 'Stupendously large' primordial black holes ruled out as a dark matter source
entry.summary: Researchers have ruled out very large primordial black holes as a source of dark matter. These hypothetical black holes would have formed from dense matter in the early universe.

entry.title: [Asteroids & comets] Backward world? Rubin finds a retrograde object past Neptune
entry.summary: The Rubin Observatory found a new object orbiting the sun past Neptune. This object has a retrograde orbit, meaning it moves in a different direction than most planets.

entry.title: [Astrobiology] Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
entry.summary: Astronomers are using computer models to simulate what a planet's atmosphere looks like if it has no life. This helps them tell the difference between empty rocky planets and those that might be inhabited.

entry.title: [Asteroids & comets] A Mysterious Asteroid Is Accelerating in Space, And We're Running Out of Explanations
entry.summary: Scientists have observed a mysterious asteroid that is speeding up as it moves through space. Researchers are currently looking for explanations for what is causing this acceleration.

entry.title: [Planets & moons] Earth's gravity may have kept the early moon's volcanic heart beating
entry.summary: New research suggests that Earth's gravity might have helped keep the early moon's volcanic center active. This challenges the idea that the moon cooled down very quickly after it formed.

entry.title: [Galaxies & cosmology] Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
entry.summary: Researchers have proposed a new theory where the universe is 26.7 billion years old. This model suggests the universe does not need dark matter or dark energy to work.

entry.title: [Planets & moons] A Stinky Gas Seeping From The Bowels of Mars May Reveal The Planet Is Still Volcanically Active
entry.summary: Scientists have detected a smelly gas seeping from Mars. This could mean that the planet is still volcanically active.

entry.title: [Galaxies & cosmology] Untangling the patterns of the cosmic microwave background to better understand the early universe
entry.summary: Scientists are studying patterns in the cosmic microwave background radiation. This helps them learn more about how the early universe formed.

entry.title: [Other] On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
entry.summary: In 1572, a German astronomer saw a supernova using only his eyes. At the time, people thought they were seeing a brand new star.
